headline: Gituamba Girls Erupts as Urban Gang Tour Brings the Festival of Colours
dek: A full day of showcases, a runway, and a national broadcast turned GITCHEZ into the loudest school day of the term.
body: Gituamba Girls High School hosted the Urban Gang Tour for a Cultural Day and Festival of Colours that ran from morning assembly to a packed evening finale. Students competed across every kind of talent — music, dance, spoken word, comedy and modelling — while the mentorship pods ran sessions alongside the main stage.

Hosts Eugine Micah and Lucy Ogunde anchored the day for Urban News on PPP TV Kenya, interviewing performers, teachers, and the eventual category winners. The modelling runway, directed with Synapse Models, closed with the crowning of Miss of the Institution by the school administration.
The feature aired nationally on Urban News, carrying the school’s name and its students far beyond Kiambu County.

headline: Loreto Kiambu Girls Turns Out in Full Colour for the Urban Gang Tour
dek: The tour’s June run opened at Loreto Kiambu with showcases, pods, and a runway finale.
body: Loreto Kiambu Girls High School welcomed the Urban Gang Tour for a full production day, complete with stage, sound, and a thirty-person crew. Music, dance, spoken word, and comedy showcases filled the programme as students competed for their categories.

The mentorship pods drew large groups between performances, delivering the mentorship half of the tour’s promise. Eugine and Lucy hosted throughout, with the day captured for a national Urban News feature.

headline: Senior Chief Koinange Girls Kicks Off the 2026 Tour
dek: The 2026 second-term tour launched at Senior Chief Koinange Girls to a roaring crowd.
body: The Urban Gang Tour opened its 2026 second-term calendar at Senior Chief Koinange Girls, setting the tone for the stops that followed. MC Paps warmed up the hall before the first performances, and the crowd stayed loud through to the final crowning.
Every moment was filmed for Urban News, giving the school a national platform and the tour a strong start to the season.

headline: Next Stop: Lari Boys High School as Bookings Stay Open
dek: The tour heads to Lari Boys High School in Kimende next, with more institutions still able to book this term.
body: Lari Boys High School in Kimende is the next confirmed stop on the Urban Gang Tour calendar, set for 19 July. Preparations are already underway with the school administration to plan the day to the minute.

Bookings for the remainder of the term remain open to schools, campuses, and event organisers who want the full production and a national Urban News feature. Institutions can request a date through the tour’s booking page.

headline: Ngeya Girls Locks In 24 July as Naivasha Gets Its First Stop
dek: The tour crosses into Nakuru County with a full production day confirmed for Ngeya Girls’ Secondary School.
body: Ngeya Girls’ Secondary School in Naivasha has confirmed 24 July for its Urban Gang Tour stop — the first time the 2026 run leaves Kiambu County.
The full format travels with it: morning pods, tree planting with Delo Greens, talent competitions, the Synapse runway, and a crowning — all filmed for Urban News.

headline: St. Augustine Mlolongo Confirms 28 July — Machakos Joins the Map
dek: Four days after Naivasha, the convoy turns towards Machakos County.
body: St. Augustine Secondary School in Mlolongo has locked 28 July, stretching the second-term run across three counties.
The administration has asked for a heavy careers focus in the pods — digital literacy and creative-economy sessions are being lined up alongside the main stage.

headline: Double Header in Maai Mahiu: Boys and Girls Editions Being Scheduled
dek: Two schools, one town — dates being finalised for late July and August.
body: Maai Mahiu Boys and Maai Mahiu Girls are both on the calendar with dates being set — a first for the tour: back-to-back editions in one town.
Expect a cross-school rivalry storyline on Urban News when the dates drop.

headline: Dr. Kiano Boys Enters the August Pipeline in Murang’a
dek: Githiga, Kangema is getting the full experience — the paperwork is moving.
body: Dr. Kiano Boys High School in Githiga, Kangema is in advanced planning for an August stop, taking the tour into Murang’a County for the first time.
The school’s drama and music clubs are already prepping entries for the talent competitions.

headline: Goshen Group of Schools and Achego Girls on the 2026 Radar
dek: Nakuru and Kisumu counties are calling — the wishlist keeps growing.
body: Goshen Group of Schools (Nakuru) and Achego Girls (Muhoroni, Kisumu) have opened booking conversations for third term.
Schools that want a 2026 date are being advised to book now — the calendar is filling fast.

headline: On The Mic: How Eugine Micah Turned a School Hall Into National Television
dek: The co-founder and lead host on building the loudest youth platform in the country.
body: Eugine Micah built the Urban Gang Tour from a single school hall into a travelling production with a national broadcast — and he is still the first voice on the mic at every stop.
As lead host of Urban News on PPP TV Kenya, he turns every school day into television, carrying student names to a national audience.
His rule for the crew is simple: the students are the stars; we are the amplifier.

headline: Lucy Ogunde: The Voice Every School Trusts
dek: Co-founder, co-host, and the reason first-time performers dare to walk on stage.
body: Lucy Ogunde anchors the parts of the day nobody forgets — the interviews, the pep talks behind the runway curtain, the crowning.
On camera for Urban News she leads with warmth and lands with authority — which is exactly why principals, parents and students all trust the tour with their biggest day.

headline: Inside the Runway: Synapse Models and the Making of Mr & Miss
dek: How a T-shaped stage and a coaching squad turn first-time walkers into the stars of the term.
body: Every crowning starts days earlier — Synapse Models and Head of Modelling Esther Wambui Gakunju coach student models through cultural, creative and professional wear categories before the big walk.
By the time the crown lands, the whole school knows every walker’s name. That is the point.

headline: Two Decks, One Road: Carian & Xavi Keep the Tour Loud
dek: The XP Hub selectors reading every crowd from gate-open to pack-down.
body: DJ Carian and DJ Xavi split the day between them — warm-up sets, competition beds, hype-set drops and the closing run — without ever letting the field go quiet.
Both ride with The Experience Hub, which is why a school field at 2 PM sounds like a Friday night headline show.

headline: Shot By Vibes: MC Dinjo’s Studio Is the Tour’s Eye
dek: The Vibe Studios joins as official photography partner — every iconic frame, theirs.
body: The Vibe Studios, led by MC Dinjo, is now the tour’s official photography partner — the stills you see on posters, recaps and this very page come out of their lenses.
Their brief is simple: catch the moment a student realises the whole school is screaming their name.

headline: One School, One Grove: The Delo Greens Tree Count Keeps Climbing
dek: Every stop leaves something growing — inside the students and on the compound.
body: Straight after the morning pods at every stop, students plant trees on their own school grounds with Delo Green Movement, led by CEO King Tae (Justus Abuko).
Hands in the soil, names on the saplings — a legacy that will outlive every scoreboard.

headline: The Heart at the Gate: How Moyo Response Keeps 3,000 Students Safe
dek: First aid stations, crowd sweeps and trained responders — the quiet department that lets the loud day happen.
body: Moyo — Swahili for heart — is what Moyo Response brings to every stop: on-site emergency cover from gate-open to pack-down.
It is the reason the tour can promise schools a duty of care in writing, not just in spirit.

headline: The Roaming Mascot Has Entered the Chat
dek: An unnamed legend in a suit is stealing scenes at every stop — and nobody knows who is inside.
body: A mascot has started appearing at tour stops — photobombing runway shots, leading chants, and losing dance showcases on purpose.
The crew refuses to confirm who is inside the suit. The students have theories. Urban News is investigating.
